$comment: Shared response-field invalidation vectors (ADR 0007). The Go and TypeScript runtimes must render every tag byte for byte. value is the JSON text of the value a consumer passes to the invalidation; a runtime reads it into its own native value (a string, an integer, a boolean) before rendering. responses[].body is the JSON text of a stored success body; tags is what each declared invalidation field tags it with, and a field absent from tags tags nothing. propertySchemas pins which response property schemas an invalidation field may name: comparable is true when both runtimes tag the same value, and every contract check (both strict readers and both providers) refuses a field whose schema is not comparable.

values.name: a string renders as its JSON string
a string escapes the quote, the backslash and the C0 controls the way JSON.stringify does
the empty string is a value
an integer renders as its decimal digits
a negative integer keeps its sign
a wide unsigned integer keeps every digit
the widest signed integer keeps every digit

refused.name: a fraction has no lexeme a TypeScript runtime keeps
null matches nothing a response can be tagged with
an array is not a scalar
an object is not a scalar

responses.name: each declared field tags the stored answer with its canonical value; null, absent, fractional and composite values tag nothing
only the declared fields tag the answer
a body that is not a JSON object tags nothing

propertySchemas.name: a string is compared as its JSON string
a formatted string stays a string in both runtimes
a string enumeration is a string
an integer of any width is compared as its digits
a nullable boolean is a boolean; null tags nothing
base64 octets decode to a byte array in TypeScript, which no invalidation value can equal
raw octets are no value either runtime compares
a number is a double in TypeScript, which keeps no lexeme
an array names no single value
an object names no single value
a union names no single kind
opaque JSON names no single kind
